image_description: A close-up view of a large whale breaching or surfacing in dark ocean water. The whale has a dark grey, mottled skin with white patches (barnacles/callosities) on its head and rostrum. Notably, there is a bright orange object attached to the side of the whale's head/neck area, resembling a tracking tag or buoy. The body appears robust and spindle-shaped. No dorsal fin is visible, consistent with grey whales, though the posterior back is partially obscured by water spray.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rostrum is visible and arched, but the top of the head where blowholes would be is angled away from the camera and obscured by the angle of the breach. Blowholes are not clearly visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skin texture clearly shows the characteristic mottled grey pattern with distinct white callosities/barnacle patches on the head and jawline.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The posterior back is largely submerged or obscured by splash/water interaction. While no dorsal fin is seen, the 'knuckles' cannot be verified due to occlusion.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the body exhibits the correct robust, thick morphology typical of a baleen whale.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Consistent with the head checkpoints, the body skin shows appropriate mottling and texture.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed; baleen plates are internal and not visible in this external shot.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The pectoral fins are submerged or out of frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is completely out of frame/submerged.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin on the head and upper body clearly displays the rough, bumpy texture associated with callosities.

artifact_observations.reasoning: There is a bright orange, geometric object attached to the whale. While this could be a real scientific tracking tag, in AI-generated images, such high-contrast, perfectly geometric objects often indicate a failure to render natural textures or an hallucination of an object. It looks slightly 'pasted on' with soft edges blending into the wet skin.
The splash and foam around the whale have a slightly smudged, painterly quality rather than crisp droplet definition, common in diffusion models.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the species is indeed a Grey Whale and not a Humpback or Right Whale, given the visual similarities in head shape and callosities.
To analyze the orange object for signs of AI hallucination (e.g., lack of physical attachment logic, weird shading) and assess the realism of the water splashes.
To check for edge bleeding between the dark whale skin and the dark water, ensuring the silhouette is coherent and not melting.

Species confirmation: Distinguishing Grey Whale features from other baleen whales.
